title: Polynomial reduction of diagonal derived Hom
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Choose a polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and put $C=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)[n]\in D(A)$, with the $A$-action by precomposition. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$ and $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$, and give $A$ its $B$-module structure by multiplication. Let $T\in D(A)$ be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and have finite Tor amplitude over $R$: some integers $a\le b$ satisfy $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R$-module $Q$ and $i\notin[a,b]$. Then there is an isomorphism, natural in $T$, in $D(A)$
$$\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B)\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T).$$
Here $\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}$ is restriction along the coprojection $A\to B$, not along multiplication $B\to A$. No diagonal dualizing condition on $T$ is assumed.

The reduction itself is derived in report.md, not claimed to be verbatim in these tags.

proof.text: For $A=0$ both sides are zero. Otherwise write $A_1,A_2$ for the two copies of $A$, $S=A_1\otimes_RP=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $q:S\to B=A_1\otimes_RA_2$, and $e=\mu q$, with $\mu$ multiplication. If $a_j$ is the image of $x_j$, then $e(x_j)=a_j$ and $e|_{A_1}=1_A$. Set $D=C_{P\to A_2}(P)$, $E=C_q(S)$, and $V=S\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}T$. All final restrictions use $A_1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-diagonal-dual-base-change]. It gives $B$ perfect over $S$, $E\cong B\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}D$ in $D(B)$, and $\operatorname{Res}_q(A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E)\cong\operatorname{Res}_eD$ in $D(S)$, with precisely the graph action through $e$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-perfect-algebra-dual-evaluation], $J_E(V)\cong B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V$. Choose a flat-term K-flat $A_1$-model $F$ of $T$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its extension $S\otimes_{A_1}F$ is K-flat by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Thus [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] gives $B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\cong B\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}T$ in $D(B)$, naturally, by $b\otimes(s\otimes t)\mapsto bs\otimes t$. Its inverse is $b\otimes t\mapsto b\otimes(1\otimes t)$. Both maps are $B$-linear and commute with $1\otimes f$ for every map $f$ of the chosen models, so the comparison retains the first-copy action and naturality.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom] with $X=A$, $E=C_q(S)$ and this $V$. Steps 2--3 identify its left coefficient with the induced coefficient of the item and its right first argument with $\operatorname{Res}_eD$. Write $i:A_1\to S$ for the coefficient inclusion. Since $qi=p_1$ and $ei=1_A$, restriction along $i$ gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}B)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{A_1\to S}R\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Res}_eD,V).$$
No flatness of $A$ over $B$ is needed.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-graph-coinduction] to $e(x_j)=a_j$: it gives $C_e(V)\cong T[-n]$ in $D(A)$, with the original action. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] with ring map $e:S\to A$, $X=D$ and $Y=V$. Its displayed $D(S)$-isomorphism is
$$\operatorname{Res}_eR\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,C_e(V))\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Res}_eD,V).$$
Restrict along $i:A_1\to S$. Since $ei=1_A$, Step 4 becomes
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,T[-n])\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D[n],T)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T).$$
The shift formula follows from [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Fix the ordered graph orientation once; every comparison is natural in $T$. All hypotheses on $T$ are retained.
